chapter: Bennie Moten, Basie and the Reno
title: Moten's funeral and legacy
summary: Goodwin describes one of Kansas City's largest funerals, with Hayes's band standing guard, and Smith credits Moten with putting the city on the map.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Tell me, Crook, you told me -- you said

that the surgeon who operated on Benny left town right afterwards or nobody ever saw him again, he went to Washington, D.C. What was the feeling throughout the jazz world, the black world and also the white world where there were jazz lovers when Benny died? It must have been quite a shock.
Well, it was one of the largest turnouts --
For the funeral?
-- of any black or white.
Benny is buried here in Kansas City?

Yes. We had -- well sort of a military-like funeral. This whole band that was created by Thamon Hayes after the Mo ten band, you know, shelled these others out, well this particular band was called upon to stand in intervals at the head and foot of Benny's casket; two men would stand all during the ceremony, would stand at the ends of the casket until the funeral -- the service was over and after this, well Benny was buried but as I say, it was one of the largest funerals that Kansas City had seen.
Were there many political figures present like Pendergast Pentakast or his brother or any of those; McElroy, any of those?
Well, maybe one or two. Benny wasn't so much of a politician.
No, but he had made such a name for
Kansas City --
Well he had made so many friends -- there were so many people there, you know; both black and white.
Well, we're still playing 'Moton Swing' every night. There had to be something he did right, you know.
Oh yeah.
He put Kansas City music on the map I think.
Yeah, definitely, definitely. He was the greatest band around, there's no question about it.
You want to add anything to this, Baby, about Benny Moton?
Well, no.
About the funeral, were you at the funeral?
No, I wasn't at the funeral.
Yes, you were.
No I wasn't.
